source.title: MTFM: A Scalable and Alignment-free Foundation Model for Industrial Recommendation in Meituan
source.authors: Xin Song; Zhilin Guan; Rui-Dong Han; Bin Tang; Tianwen Chen; Bing Li; Zi-Hao Li; Han Zhang; Fei Jiang; Qing Wang; Zikang Xu; Fengyi Li; Chunzhen Jing; Lei Yu; Wei-Bin Lin

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some tables and figures are text-extracted, and ACM conference and DOI placeholders remain.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling behavior in an industrial recommendation model, a training regime beyond language-model pretraining, using model-scale and training-data sweeps.
record.gate_note: The paper measures recommendation GAUC across model scales and training-token volumes. It does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy, predict larger language-model runs from smaller ones, or test a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Other reported comparisons, including overall model benchmarks and attention-efficiency experiments, do not test the listed scaling-law versions.
record.test_reason: It sweeps model compute (10x–70x MMoE inference GFLOPs) and training-data volume for a transformer recommendation model and reports a fitted scaling trend in CTCVR GAUC. That is a scaling result in a regime beyond text pretraining (V5). The metric is a ranking AUC rather than loss, and the fitted functional form is not stated.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors claim MTFM shows 'robust scaling laws with consistent slopes' in CTCVR GAUC gain over an MMoE baseline as inference compute grows from 10x to 70x. They also claim GAUC rises with training tokens for three model sizes, with the gap between sizes widening. They do not specify a power-law fit.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an industrial recommendation model and CTCVR GAUC rather than language models and held-out cross-entropy; sweeps model scale and training data but does not test the original loss-law or compute-optimal-allocation recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported model-scale slopes differ by scenario (R² values: SQS 0.9952, HP 0.9833, PHF 0.9368); the training-data scaling comparison uses three model sizes.
record.problems: Scaling values are presented in figures rather than tabulated; the text does not give parameter counts, fitted exponents, fitting procedures, or uncertainty estimates for the scaling results. The model-scale figure uses relative inference GFLOPs, not a stated parameter-count sweep.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were omitted. Other benchmark, attention-efficiency, and online A/B results do not measure the scaling behaviors named by the versions.

untested.parts: No extrapolation from small fits to larger runs.
No fixed-parameter shape sweep. Table 3 varies attention type with differing compute and throughput.

Untested parts: the explicit power-law functional form and exponents, loss rather than GAUC, parameter-count sweeps, separate-run data scaling, and image/video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer.
Not tested; GAUC is the training-objective metric itself, not a separate downstream task.

missing.what: The functional form of the Figure 4(a) fit and its slope/exponent values per scenario. The text only says the slopes are 'consistent', which a cross-study comparison needs quantified.
Observation that the gap between model sizes widens as training tokens increase.

record.verdict_notes: An industrial recommendation paper. The scaling section is short and figure-only, and the main contributions are architecture and efficiency. The V5 support rests on R² values of an unspecified fit. The data-scaling evidence is within-run training curves, so it cannot establish a power-law form.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or language-model parameter, token, or compute sweep.
No prediction of larger runs from fits on smaller runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or comparison of parameter and token growth rates.
The attention-configuration comparison is not a test of language-model loss at fixed parameter count.
Tests scaling in industrial recommendation using CTCVR GAUC and plotted model/data scales; does not test other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream-task performance prediction from pretraining loss or model scale.
Does not test dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations on fitting choices, nor report curve bending away from a power law.

relation.reason: The paper discusses scaling laws and reports scalability trends, without specifying a functional form that tests the catalog's power-law claim.

tranche.reason: The reported experiments establish recommendation-performance improvements with inference compute and continual training, but do not identify or test the power-law form required by V5. Under the supplied definitions, related scalability measurements alone do not test that version.

source_check.notes: The extracted Figure 4(a) preserves R² values 0.9952, 0.9833 and 0.9368 but loses explicit scenario-to-value associations. Figure 4(b) describes continual-training trajectories, with no fitted law or numerical trajectory values preserved.
